about.title: Ripon Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Ripon residents often travel to larger San Joaquin County facilities for surgery, emergency care, or specialist treatment, and most of those visits go fine. But when a diagnosis is missed, a medication is mishandled, or a surgical step is skipped, the effects can follow a patient home to Ripon for months or years. California law recognizes that not every bad outcome is malpractice — a claim generally requires showing that a provider departed from the accepted standard of care and that this departure caused harm. Because these cases involve technical medical records and strict filing deadlines under California's MICRA statute, having someone review the details early matters. We don't charge any fee; we simply review Ripon patients' and families' medical situations so they can get a clear read on whether their case may qualify for a claim.

items.title: Deadlines Are Strict and Specific
items.desc: California generally allows one year from when the harm is discovered, and no more than three years from the injury itself, plus a required 90-day pre-suit notice — we can help track these dates before they close a door.

items.title: Expert Review Is Almost Always Required
items.desc: Because a qualified medical expert typically must weigh in on whether care fell below the accepted standard, reviewing your case early gives that evaluation time to happen properly.

items.title: Non-Economic Damages Are Capped, But the Cap Rises Yearly
items.desc: MICRA places a statutory limit on non-economic damages that increases annually, so understanding current figures matters when weighing a claim's value.

items.question: I had a bad outcome after treatment near Ripon — does that automatically mean malpractice happened?
items.answer: No. California law is clear that a poor result by itself isn't proof of malpractice; the question is whether the provider's care fell below the accepted medical standard and caused the harm. We can review your medical records to see whether that standard was likely met or missed.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a medical malpractice claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, you have one year from when you discover the injury, but never more than three years from when it occurred, and a 90-day pre-suit notice is usually required before filing. Because Ripon patients often receive care at facilities outside city limits, tracking exactly when treatment records were created can affect these dates, so it's worth checking sooner rather than later.

items.question: Does it cost anything to have our team review my case?
items.answer: No. We provide a free case review, and we work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover. We handle your case directly and will evaluate it to help you understand your options.
